chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ala'a ibn al-Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Venerate your companions and dignify them, and let not some of you attack others, nor harm one another, nor envy one another; and beware of stinginess. Be the servants of God, the sincere, the righteous.'

key_terms.الصَّالِحِينَ: The righteous — those who do good deeds and fulfill their obligations
key_terms.الْبُخْلَ: Stinginess, miserliness — withholding what one has from those who need it
key_terms.الْمُخْلَصِينَ: The sincere/purified ones — those whose worship is free of hypocrisy
key_terms.تَحَاسَدُوا: Envy one another — from hasad, considered a destructive spiritual vice
key_terms.تَضَارُّوا: Mutually harm — reciprocal form, emphasizing that harm flows both ways
key_terms.عَظِّمُوا: Venerate, hold in high esteem — active showing of honor and respect
key_terms.وَقِّرُوهُمْ: Dignify, show reverence — from waqar (dignity, gravitas)
key_terms.يَتَهَجَّمْ: Intrude upon, attack — the root tahaggama implies forceful, unwelcome intrusion

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about respecting companions and avoiding envy and stinginess?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), as reported by Imam al-Sadiq, repeatedly exhorted his followers to honor their companions, avoid harmful and destructive behaviors — aggression, mutual harm, and envy — and to beware of the vice of stinginess. He concluded by calling on them to embody the highest qualities of sincere and righteous worship. This teaching was addressed to the early Shia community in Medina and Kufa, who faced both social pressures and internal communal tensions; the Imam's repeated exhortations ('كَانَ يَقُولُ' — he used to say) indicate this was a persistent pastoral concern.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ala’a Bin Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Venerate your companions and dignify them, and you should neither attack each other, nor harm, nor envy (each other); and beware of the stinginess. Become the servants of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the sincere, the righteous’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ala’ ibn al-Fudayl from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) would say, ‘Show respect for your friends and dignify them. Do not be aggressive to each other, do not harm or envy each other. Beware of stinginess and be sincere and righteous servants of Allah.’”
